column1: # THE UNIT IS THE CAMERONIANS (SCOTTISH RIFLES). The surrounding pages of the same return are full of
# Scottish names and Scottish birthplaces - Malcolm Campbell, Duncan Sinclair, and men born at Glasgow,
# Lanarkshire, Dunbartonshire, Ayrshire, Roxburghshire, Kirkcudbright. A Hertfordshire farm labourer's
# son among them is unusual and is exactly the sort of thing the regular army did.
# WHY THIS IS PROBABLE AND NOT PROVED, and the page says so:
#   FOR   the birthplace is BALDOCK, which is not a common birthplace outside Hertfordshire
#   FOR   the age excludes the other two Baldock Freds: the Norton End boy of the second family would
#         be 23, and the 17 Orchard Road man born 10 April 1887 would be 24 AND IS AT BALDOCK THAT NIGHT
#   AGAINST  the entry gives FREDERICK, not Frederick James
#   AGAINST  it rests on ONE census age and ONE birthplace, and this archive has been wrong three times
#            in a week by treating a good fit as a finding
# WHAT IT CHANGES. The 1921 census holds exactly ONE Baldock-born Frederick Castle in the whole of
# England and Wales, and it is the OTHER family's man. Ours is out of the country by 1921, is in no
# death index, and is not in Soldiers Died in the Great War. A regular soldier of 1911 who vanishes
# like that was posted abroad and stayed, or died in a service Soldiers Died does not cover.
# NEXT: the Cameronians' medal rolls and service papers for a Frederick Castle.
